title: King Ambarisha's senses
hook: a king who could have any pleasure gives each of his senses to God, and it's why a puja has a lamp, a bell, incense, flowers and food
carry: master the senses by offering them

segments.voice: Yesterday: bhuta-jaya, and Hanuman's way: power in God's service. All eight powers, and he called himself a servant.

You met King Ambarisha on day one thirty, keeping his Ekadashi fast while an angry sage raged. The Bhagavata says he ruled the whole earth. Any pleasure a king could want was his for the asking. Here's what he did with his senses. His eyes he gave to seeing Vishnu's images. His ears, to hearing Vishnu's stories. His hands, to cleaning Vishnu's temple. His nose, to the scent of tulsi from Vishnu's feet. And his tongue, to tasting food first offered to God.
screen: `A KING WITH EVERY PLEASURE.` → `EYES, EARS, HANDS.` → `EVERY SENSE GIVEN TO GOD.`

segments.voice: Ambarisha didn't shut his senses down. He turned them. That's the Hindu teaching about the senses. The Katha Upanishad calls them horses: strong, and the work is to steer them, not to kill them. Patanjali calls it indriya-jaya, mastery of the senses. Sutra 3.47: by samyama on the senses in five aspects, mastery. Not just what you see, but the seeing itself; the sense of me that says I see; and what the senses are for. Sutra 3.48: from that comes a swiftness like the mind, and mastery over nature itself. One way to read book three: it walks from the outside in. yesterday the elements, what's known; today the senses, the knowing; tomorrow, the one who knows. The devotional path does it Ambarisha's way. Look at a Hindu puja: a lamp for the eyes, a bell for the ears, incense and flowers for the nose, food offered and shared back as prasad for the tongue, sandal paste and flowers, offered by hand, for touch. Many teachers read it as every sense brought to God at once. Now the week. Dattatreya's wasp. Dhruva's steady star. Hanuman's heart. The walker on water. Shankara in a king's body. Hanuman's service. And Ambarisha. A week of powers, and every story points past them. Today your senses get pulled all day, by screens built to catch them. Ambarisha's answer isn't to close your eyes. It's to give them something worth seeing.
screen: `AMBARISHA: SENSES TURNED, NOT SHUT.` · `THE KATHA: SENSES AS HORSES.` · `INDRIYA-JAYA: MASTERY OF SENSES.` · `LAMP, BELL, INCENSE, PRASAD.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `MASTER THE SENSES BY OFFERING THEM.`

segments.voice: If you have a lamp or a candle, light it; if not, picture one. Give it your eyes for a moment. Then your ears: one sound around you. Then smell, taste and touch: the air, your own mouth, your hands resting. If you pray, offer each sense to God as you go, the way Ambarisha did. If you don't, simply give each one your full attention.
Indriya-jaya, mastery of the senses. By samyama on the senses in five aspects, it brings a swiftness like the mind's own.
Your line: master the senses by offering them. Ambarisha turned every one toward God. A week of the powers, done.
